title: Checkpoint prep: audit questions + evidence plan (scratch)
content:
Purpose: quick scratchpad for the 1:1 with Sam (external auditor) and follow-ups with internal owners. Want to leave meeting with: 1) agreed evidence list, 2) owners and dates for missing artifacts, 3) decision on vendor evidence scope (third-party attestations vs. our compensating controls).

Agenda (15-20 min):
- 0-3m: TLDR status (controls mapped, gap count)
- 3-8m: auditor questions we expect (see below)
- 8-14m: evidence handoff plan + format/filters
- 14-18m: vendor scoping clarifications
- last 2 min: confirm next sync and quick action list

Expected auditor questions (prep answers):
- Access control: list of SSO providers, MFA enforcement date ranges, evidence = Okta org settings export + last 90d login report (owner: IAM team, due: 2026-03-17)
- Change control: example PR -> merged release pipeline trace for service 'router' (owner: release-eng, due: 2026-03-22)
- Encryption: KMS account mapping + key policies (owner: infra-sec, due: 2026-03-18)
- Vendor risk: for DB hosting provider ask for SOC2 report or our vendor risk assessment (owner: vendor-risk squad, due: 2026-03-24)

Evidence checklist (quick):
- Okta org settings export (CSV)
- MFA enrollment policy screenshots + policy doc link
- Last 3 deploy PRs + pipeline logs for canary rollout
- KMS key rotation records
- Vendor contracts summary + latest attestation PDF
- Incident postmortem sample (redacted) - pick a <6mo one
- SRE runbook that shows oncall escalation (linked)

Notes-to-self:
- Avoid over-sharing raw logs; auditor prefers curated extracts with date ranges and a short explanation of how the artifact proves the control.
- If auditor asks for user lists, provide csv of role/teams not full profile data. PII minimization.
- Tag each artifact filename with control id (e.g., AC-2_Okta_2026-03-10.csv)

Vendor risk follow-ups:
- Confirm whether auditor accepts vendor SOC2+bridge letter vs. full questionnaire. If they require questionnaire, route to vendor-risk lead now.
- For small infra vendors (no attestation), prepare compensating controls doc (network segmentation diagrams + our monitoring coverage).

Open questions / parking lot: (to clarify in meeting)
- Sam: do you need historical evidence beyond 12 months for any control? (we think no, but confirm)
- Backup verification cadence—auditor asked about random restores; do we have a one-off restore runbook and owner? (ask SRE)
- Does auditor want raw deployment manifests or just build artifacts + pipeline trace?

Action items (post-meeting plan):
- [Kai] Collate evidences to shared secure folder and name by control id (due 2026-03-12)
- [Avery] Export Okta reports + MFA proof, redact PII (due 2026-03-17)
- [Jordan] Draft vendor list + attach latest certs/attestations (due 2026-03-16)
- [Release-eng lead] Provide PR+pipeline trace for example change (due 2026-03-22)
- [Infra-sec] Produce KMS key policy snippet + rotation log (due 2026-03-18)

Draft message to auditor (one-liner to send after meeting):
"Thanks Sam — following our call I uploaded the agreed artifacts to the secure folder (link). Items are named by control id; please flag anything missing and I'll route immediately to the owner."

Quick checklist when packaging artifacts:
- Include short cover note per artifact explaining purpose and relevant control id
- Redact user-identifying fields except for service accounts (include a mapping file)
- Zip artifacts and put checksum in tile; send access via secure link only

Reminders:
- Keep copies of every artifact in compliance archive (s3://redwood-compliance-archive/2026-q1/)
- Log auditor access (who downloaded what) for future evidence of cooperation

Potential blockers:
- Vendor hasn't provided current attestation -> escalate to vendor-risk and legal
- Release-eng backlog might delay PR trace extraction -> get a short commit list first

Follow-up meeting: target 2026-03-19 (15 min) to confirm outstanding items and handoffs.
